item.text:
**1B.7 Research Note: Sheikh Hasina in 2024**

Bottom line: the 2024 public record **leans positive on institution-building**, but with meaningful criticism that Rooppur and nuclear governance still suffered from **prestige politics, corruption risk, and weak regulatory capacity**. I did **not** find direct 2024 proof that Hasina personally filled nuclear/security decisions with ideologues, but I did find credible criticism that merit and independent oversight were insufficient.

**Positive evidence**
- **Bangladesh committed to non-proliferation, peaceful nuclear use: FM** | Publisher: BSS | Date: April 30, 2024 | URL: https://www.bssnews.net/news-flash/186546 | Summary: The foreign minister said Bangladesh would keep the highest safety and security standards for its nuclear plants and welcomed IAEA support for training and safeguards. This is direct evidence of investment in expertise and institutions. | QIDs: 1B.7, 1B.4, 1B.3
- **Bangladesh nuclear regulators train at Russia’s Novovoronezh NPP** | Publisher: Nuclear Engineering International | Date: June 18, 2024 | URL: https://www.neimagazine.com/news/bangladesh-nuclear-regulators-train-at-russias-novovoronezh-npp/ | Summary: BAERA inspectors were trained with Russian regulator support, and the article says this was the fourth group of specialists to receive such training. That supports the view that Bangladesh was building technical regulatory capacity rather than relying only on patronage. | QIDs: 1B.7, 1B.3
- **Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant : 48 Bangladeshi specialists complete pre-licensing training** | Publisher: Daily Country Today | Date: July 8, 2024 | URL: https://dailycountrytodaybd.com/story/rooppur-nuclear-power-plant-%3A-48-bangladeshi-specialists-complete-pre-licensing-training | Summary: Forty-eight specialists completed pre-licensing training and still had to obtain licenses from BAERA. The piece shows a formal competence-and-licensing pipeline for operators, which is the kind of institutional investment this question looks for. | QIDs: 1B.7, 1B.3
- **Home | Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority** | Publisher: BAERA | Date: November 3-7, 2024 | URL: https://baera.gov.bd/ | Summary: The BAERA homepage snippet records a National Training Course on Safeguards held November 3-7, 2024. This is official evidence that the regulator was running safeguards training inside the state institution. | QIDs: 1B.7, 1B.3, 1B.4

**Critical evidence**
- **Is Bangladesh’s ‘nuclear prestige’ an illusion?** | Publisher: The Daily Star | Date: April 20, 2024 | URL: https://www.thedailystar.net/opinion/views/news/bangladeshs-nuclear-prestige-illusion-3590666 | Summary: This opinion piece argues the second-plant push looked prestige-driven at a time of financial stress, debt, and inflation. It is not direct proof of loyalist staffing, but it is credible criticism that decision-making may have been too politicized and image-oriented. | QIDs: 1B.7, 1B.1
- **Billions at Stake: Unveiling the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant's Spiraling Costs and Corruption** | Publisher: Bangla Outlook | Date: April 23, 2024 | URL: https://en.banglaoutlook.org/news/1099 | Summary: The piece alleges major cost inflation and the accumulation of politically linked ancillary contracts around Rooppur. That supports a concern that project governance was vulnerable to patronage and weak discipline rather than pure technical merit. | QIDs: 1B.7, 1B.3
- **Rooppur Power Plant a white elephant in energy sector: Experts** | Publisher: TBS News | Date: October 5, 2024 | URL: https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/energy/rooppur-power-plant-was-al-govts-white-elephant-energy-sector-experts-958801 | Summary: Experts described Rooppur as a white-elephant project tied to mismanagement and corruption under the Awami League government. This is broader than nuclear staffing alone, but it is relevant criticism that the project was not being governed as a purely technocratic institution. | QIDs: 1B.7, 1B.3

**Search gap**
- I searched directly for 2024 evidence of loyalist/ideological capture versus expert-led nuclear governance.
- I found **no direct 2024 source** showing Hasina explicitly surrounding nuclear/security decisions with loyalists or ideologues.
- The strongest negative evidence is **critique of management and procurement**, not a documented case of ideological appointment in the nuclear chain of command.

**Synthesis**
- Best-supported read: **some real investment in expertise and institutions, but not a clean technocratic record**.
- The official and operator-training evidence is substantial.
- The criticism is also substantial, but it mostly targets **prestige politics, corruption, and weak governance**, not a documented ideological capture of nuclear/security decision-making.
